pageProps.title: Unpack the images from super.img
pageProps.review: Summarizes the detailed process of converting an Android Super Image to raw, extracting each partition image, and loop mounting them using the simg2img and lpunpack tools, which are AOSP build results.
pageProps.content:
## Unpack the images from super.img
- When you build AOSP, host tools are also built.
- Since the Super Image is a Sparse image, it must be converted to raw before unpacking.
- The file system varies according to ```BOARD_*_FILE_SYSTEM_TYPE```, and in the case of ext4, it can be mounted with ```mount -t ext4```.
- If it's <mark>erofs</mark>, a separate tool (e.g., erofsfuse) is required for mounting.

1. You need to convert the Sparse Image to a raw image.
```sh
{
    "title": "Sparse image to raw image"
}
---
$ file super.img
super.img: Android sparse image, version 1.0, Total of...
  
$ out/host/linux-x86/bin/simg2img super.img super_raw.img
  
$ file super_raw.img
super_raw.img: data
```
2. You need to extract the Super Image, which consists of multiple partitions.
```sh
{
    "title": "Extracting partition images from super"
}
---
$ out/host/linux-x86/bin/lpunpack super_raw.img extracted
$ ls extracted
oom_a.img   product_b.img   system_dlkm_a.img ...
```
3. The file system of the images will appear as ext4, and you must add the offset option for mounting.
```sh
{
    "title": "Loop mount with offset options"
}
---
$ mkdir vendor
$ sudo mount -t ext4 -o loop,ro,offset=0 vendor_a.img vendor
$ ls vendor
apex   bin   build.prop   etc ...
```
